lines.text: In 1968, Edsger Dike-stra argued against the go to statement.

lines.text: A jump can leave for anywhere and never come back, so you can't treat a piece of code as a black box.

lines.text: The fix was structured programming: blocks, loops and function calls, where control goes in at the top and comes out at the bottom.

lines.text: Fifty years later, in 2018, Nathaniel Smith pointed out that starting a task is the same kind of jump.
